name: Estonia
kernel_gaps: Distribution tax: company tax only when profit is paid out (22/78), none on retention, none on the shareholder; owner.py has no retention dimension (local tools/retention.py)
Income test that counts untaxed income: the § 23 hump income includes Estonian dividends taxed at company level and excludes deductions (local PIn.dividendsEE / POut.tulu)

Self-employed social tax on a circular base (profit/1.33) with a minimum charge (12 x kuumaar) and a ceiling (10 x 12 minimum wages); Contribution has a threshold floor, not a minimum charge (local EeTax.fie)
Monthly withholding with the exemption claimed at one payer and an annual true-up for uneven streams (perPeriod covers only even streams; local Withholding.lean)
Versioned parameters in one exe (input year 2026: flat 8,400 exemption)

validation.referee: OECD TW 2025 (Taxing Wages 2026, year 2025) country table
validation.notes: 48/48 mapped lines (CGTC, CGITLETC, CGITFP, SLT, EECSSC, CTGG) exact (within 1 euro; S100 and S67 within 0.01 euro, Lean oecd_S100/oecd_S67) once the OECD conventions are applied: no II-pillar payment (F1) and the single-parent allowance for SP67 (F2); the 8 raw take-home-pay lines differ by exactly the 2 % II pillar net of its 22 % deduction (e.g. -400 at S100)

validation.referee: EMTA published 2025/2026 figures (2025 changes page, exemption page)
validation.notes: training/gift relief 264, III-pillar relief 1320, exemption 7848 below 14,400 and 0 above 25,200, pension-age 9312, 2026 flat 8400, social-tax minimum 270.60/month (runs/emta_checks.txt); no official EMTA income-tax calculator found (none in the emta.ee sitemap)

validation.referee: Statute self-consistency: TuMS § 42(1) monthly formula vs § 23(2) annual (proof)
validation.notes: Lean monthly_even_bounds: for every monthly wage w, 12 x monthly exemption is within 0-11 cents of the annual exemption at 12w

headline: Estonia's 2025 flat 22 % with a basic exemption withdrawn between 14,400 and 25,200 euro reproduces all 48 compared OECD lines exactly; the 'tax hump' is a proved 37.99 % income-tax band (40.8 % with contributions) that also bites on tax-free Estonian dividends (up to 1,726.56 euro) and turns uneven monthly pay into refunds or bills of up to 1,727 euro, while an owner-manager pays 22 % through dividends against up to 43.8 % through salary and retained profit earns its return untaxed.
